To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have introduced a new method for performing meta‐analysis of neuroimaging results that takes account of the random effect size and the uncertainty in the reported effect size, and that this method is useful for meta‐analysis in neurology and neuroimaging.

(a) we have implemented a method of coordinate based random effect meta-analysis of published neuroimaging studies, (b) this method is implemented as free software and is available for download and use, and (c) we have demonstrated that this method has the potential to be a useful tool in the interpretation of published neuroimagine studies.
(i) the ClusterZ software is freely available to download and can be used for coordinate based random effect meta‐analyses and meta‐regressions of neuroimaging data.

the development of statistical methodology for neuroimaging studies that are based on the analysis of functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) or magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) data.
the analysis of neuroimaging data, in particular the analysis of functional MRI and voxel‐based morphometric data.
